Evidence/CLM-045
Evidence record

A successful cash payment is not yet durable financial use

What does this evidence establish?

World Bank/G2Px material (May 2024) describes an eight-district digital-payment pilot within Yemen's unconditional cash-transfer programme, reported to have benefited 45,460 recipients, with an emphasis on payments into fully functional accounts and recipient choice. As reported by programme partners, this indicates delivery and exposure to a formal digital service. Yemen evidence can support several links from cash delivery through usability, resilience and local financial relationships, but it does not yet establish persistent post-transfer bank-account or e-wallet use. Beneficiaries, registrations, identities and opened accounts are not measures of durable use.

What does it measure?

This record sets out a measurement gap between successful delivery of a cash transfer and continued financial use after it; its only figure is the pilot's reported number of recipients.

Who or what does it apply to?

Source-specific local/programme/project universes

When was it measured or observed?

Evidence published 2023–2026; the pilot material dates from May 2024, and the reference period of the 45,460 figure is not recorded here

How current is it?

The latest evidence in this record was published in 2026; the pilot material dates from May 2024. The record should not be read as describing later programme reach or use unless newer evidence is published.

What this evidence does not establish

Cash-transfer beneficiaries, village savings and loan associations (VSLAs), identity targets and opened accounts are not measures of durable financial use. The 45,460 figure is a programme-reported number of recipients, not a count of people who kept using an account.

Limits of the measure

Evidence is meaningful through several intermediate links; durable post-transfer account/wallet use remains unobserved.
